summary: Summation No. 20 covers South Korea under USAMGIK for May 1947. The dominant political event was the reconvening of the U.S.-U.S.S.R. Joint Commission in Seoul on 21 May after the Marshall-Molotov correspondence, with Joint Communiques Nos. 9 and 10 printed in full. The Interim Legislative Assembly wrangled over the Anticollaborator Bill and the General Franchise Law (voting age raised to 25), and Speaker Kimm Kiu Sic offered, then withdrew, his resignation. Economic coverage includes a 57.4 percent summer-grain outlook, Bank of Chosen notes at 17.4 billion yen, a 17-billion-yen budget, gold-mine reopening rules, wage reform for vested-factory workers and civil servants, trade tables, rail and utility data, a planned 20 percent ration cut and the summer-grain quota. Social sections report cholera immunization, refugee housing and the National Refugee Board, schooling, youth movements and press reaction. Historians gain primary texts of the Commission documents and statistical tables.
highlights: The U.S.-U.S.S.R. Joint Commission reconvened in Seoul on 21 May; Soviet delegates under Col. Gen. T. F. Shtikov arrived 20 May with 65 staff, and Maj. Gen. A. E. Brown led the American side.

Joint Communique No. 9 (26 May) set a ten-member Commission, weekly alternating chairmanship and three subcommissions; Communique No. 10 (1 June) recorded agreement in principle on broad consultation with Korean parties.

The Legislative Assembly raised the General Franchise Law's minimum voting age to 25, defeating a 20-year proposal 39 to 17; the Anticollaborator Bill was tabled 35 to 26 after dissenters boycotted a 26 May session, leaving no quorum.
Speaker Dr. Kimm Kiu Sic resigned on 19 May citing ill health; the Assembly rejected the resignation 52 to 0 and he agreed to reconsider.
Estimated summer grain output reached only 57.4 percent of goal (4,481,881 of 7,814,367 suk); the ration was to drop from 2.5 to 2 hop for July-August, with a 711,000-suk collection quota.

A Wage Rate and Incentive Board program rescinded the 18 June 1946 wage freeze, allowed raises up to 25 percent for about 250,000 civil servants and 250,000 vested-factory workers, and issued eight yards of cotton cloth each.

Bank of Chosen notes in circulation reached 17,417,709,259 yen on 31 May; a balanced budget of up to 17 billion yen went to the Assembly, while April spending of 1,316,841,645 yen far exceeded revenue of 616,329,439.
A National Refugee Board was created 12 May; 20,042 refugees entered in April, and by 29 May 8,329 refugee houses were complete, 6,067 under construction and 772 yet to be built.

sections.title: Front matter
sections.summary: Library flyleaves, cover of Summation No. 20 (May 1947), table of contents for Parts I-IV, and a list of 26 charts plus a Map of Korea.

sections.title: Part I: General
sections.summary: Digest of the month: Joint Commission reconvened 21 May, Assembly debated the franchise law, summer grain outlook 57.4 percent, ration to be cut 20 percent, cholera immunization and a new National Refugee Board.

sections.title: Section 1. Political Activities
sections.summary: Assembly handled the Anticollaborator Bill and Franchise Law; Dr. Kimm's resignation was rejected 52 to 0; Joint Commission reconvened 21 May; National Police Board established.

sections.title: Section 2. Economic Activities
sections.summary: Crop output at 57.4 percent of goal, coal averaging 20,927 tons monthly, Bank of Chosen notes at 17.4 billion yen, a 17-billion-yen budget and a 20 percent food ration cut.

sections.title: Section 3. Social Activities
sections.summary: Cholera immunization 90 percent complete, Korean Medical Association formed 10 May, 20,042 April refugees, 1,211 repatriated, and Seoul National University entrance rules.

sections.title: Part II: Political
sections.summary: Reorganization approved 17 May, Assembly proceedings, Marshall-Molotov letters and Joint Communiques Nos. 9 and 10; also the Civil Liberties Union, National Police Board, juvenile courts, prisons and fire losses.

sections.title: Section 1. Government and Politics
sections.summary: Reorganization plan approved 17 May, Assembly franchise debate and Kimm resignation, Marshall-Molotov letters, Joint Communiques Nos. 9 and 10, and Rhee's and Kim Koo's reservations.

sections.title: Administration
sections.summary: Military Governor approved departmental reorganization 17 May; governors met 9-10 May; property custodian made directly responsible; 3,195 of 5,916 central employees come from Seoul or Kyonggi-do.

sections.title: Korean Interim Legislative Assembly
sections.summary: Anticollaborator Bill tabled 35 to 26; Franchise Law voting age set at 25; Kimm resignation rejected 52 to 0; talks with North Korea's People's Party proposed.

sections.title: Political Developments and U.S.-U.S.S.R. Joint Commission
sections.summary: Rhee and Kim Koo withhold decision; Lyuh Woon Hyung elected Laboring People's Party chairman 24 May; Marshall-Molotov letters; Communiques Nos. 9 and 10 create three subcommissions.

sections.title: Section 2. Legal and Public Safety
sections.summary: Korean Civil Liberties Union formed 22 May; National Police Board created; juvenile courts expanded to four; 20,282 prisoners in April; April fire losses 39,951,800 yen; Marine Academy opened with 312 students.

sections.title: Part III: Economic
sections.summary: Natural resources, industry, commerce and rationing: summer grain at 57.4 percent of goal, 17.4 billion yen in notes, 258 of 614 locomotives operable, and a 20 percent ration cut, with many tables.

sections.title: Section 1. Natural Resources
sections.summary: Summer grain at 57.4 percent of goal with provincial tables, 1946 flood loss of 1.72 billion yen, coal at 20,927 tons monthly, and conditions for reopening vested gold mines.

sections.title: Section 2. Industry
sections.summary: 20-million-yen copper loan, one of three fertilizer plants working, raw silk up to 88,890 pounds in April, and the Wage Rate and Incentive Board's eight-point plan with raises up to 25 percent.

sections.title: Section 3. Commerce
sections.summary: Finance, property custody, trade with Japan, China, Hongkong and the U.S., railroads (258 of 614 locomotives operable), utility rate proposals, public works and communications statistics.

sections.title: Finance
sections.summary: Bank of Chosen notes 17,417,709,259 yen; deposits 19,993,000,000 yen in February; April spending 1,316,841,645 yen against revenue 616,329,439; budget limited to 17 billion yen.

sections.title: Property Control and Imports and Exports
sections.summary: Office of Property Custody took direct control 12 May; vested property sales 3,880,601.84 yen; National Economic Board foreign trade policy of 25 March; tables of imports from Japan and private trade.

sections.title: Transportation
sections.summary: Hongkong trade office opened 10 April; 32,944 railroad ties laid 1-20 April; railroads employ 32,366; Seoul has 257 tramcars with under 50 running.

sections.title: Public Utilities
sections.summary: Electric supply depends on North Korean power (837,678,737 kWh received); Public Utilities Committee recommends rate rises, such as freight up to 50 percent and wholesale power to 25 sen per kWh.

sections.title: Public Works
sections.summary: Highway program completed March at 200 million yen; 1,051 highway projects costing 305,199,782 yen; 1946 flood damage 6.2 billion yen; waterworks subsidies totaling 100,631,000 yen.

sections.title: Communications
sections.summary: 646 post offices, three North-South mail exchanges in May, Pusan-Fukuoka cable used from 15 May, and seven broadcasting stations with 180,185 paying households.

sections.title: Section 4. Rationing and Price Control
sections.summary: Ration to fall from 2.5 to 2 hop for July-August; summer-grain quota 711,000 suk led by Cholla-namdo with 163,000; 57 percent of fertilizer delivered; shoes at 300 yen for essential workers.

sections.title: Part IV: Social
sections.summary: Public health, education, culture and public information: cholera control, 8,329 refugee houses, Seoul National University regents, youth organizations and press reaction to the Joint Commission.

sections.title: Section 1. Public Health and Welfare
sections.summary: Cholera immunization phases, Korean Medical Association formed 10 May, LARA advisory committee, 20,042 April refugees, 8,329 refugee houses completed and 1,211 repatriates.

sections.title: Section 2. Education, Culture and Religion
sections.summary: New Seoul National University regents 27 May, 392,496 textbooks distributed, Farmers' Music Festival 23-27 May, Youth Movement at 77,930 members, and 47 missionaries in South Korea.

sections.title: Section 3. Public Information
sections.summary: 28 films released (22 American), 273,360 radio sets in a 1 May census, Farmers' Weekly circulation halved to 300,000, and press comment on the Joint Commission and Rhee.

sections.title: Map of Korea and back matter
sections.summary: Map of Korea on page 95, followed by a library due-date slip, blank scanned leaves and the digitization back cover.
